subject: Insurance
title: Climate Change: The Uninsurable Future
description: A quick win: understand Climate Change: The Uninsurable Future.

hook.text: Global insured disaster losses averaged $100 billion per year from 2020-2023. In the 1990s, the average was $20 billion.

buildup.text: Hotter temperatures, stronger storms, and rising seas are increasing losses faster than premiums can rise to cover them.

discovery.text: Insurers model future risk using historical data.

twist.text: Swiss Re estimates that climate change will cause $23 trillion in global economic losses by 2050.

climax.text: Insurance was built on predictable risk. Climate change is making risk unpredictable.

punchline.text: $100 billion a year and rising. Climate change may break the insurance model.

quiz.question: Why does climate change threaten the insurance industry?
options: Historical data no longer predicts future risk accurately
